title: Nearest-point descent proof of higher-dimensional colorful Caratheodory
description: For d+1 finite point sets in R^d, each of whose convex hulls contains the origin, conjecture that one can select one point per set forming a simplex containing the origin, reachable by a monotone descent that repeatedly swaps a single vertex on the facet nearest the origin to strictly decrease the distance from the origin to the current rainbow simplex. Formalize the distance-to-origin as a strictly decreasing potential under a well-chosen swap, prove termination, and thereby obtain a constructive proof that generalizes the one-dimensional sign argument (which reduces to: each class straddling zero yields a nonpositive and a nonnegative vertex, and opposite-sign vertices span a segment through zero).

title: Spanning as the sharp threshold for join-transfer of colorful Caratheodory
description: The colorful hypothesis constrains the vertex sets while the conclusion is read off the complexes. Conjecture that 'contains every vertex as a 0-face' (spanning) is the unique minimal monotone property of the color complexes guaranteeing the colorful conclusion transfers to the join, and that connectivity or being a positive-dimensional tree does not suffice. Build explicit non-spanning-but-connected complexes on two colors where each vertex set straddles zero yet no face of the join contains zero, extending the known point-complex counterexample, and prove a matching positive result that spanning always suffices.

title: Counting robust rainbow transversals through the origin
description: If each of d+1 color classes contains the origin with positive depth (the origin survives deletion of any single vertex from the class), conjecture the number of rainbow transversals whose simplex contains the origin is bounded below by an explicit function of the class sizes rather than merely one. Reduce, via the transversal-selection reformulation of colorful Caratheodory, to an extremal combinatorial counting problem, and prove a first nontrivial lower bound in dimension one where the sign argument is exact.

title: Matroid-colored Caratheodory over joins of spanning complexes
description: Model the color structure as a matroid whose ground set is the vertex set and whose bases are the spanning faces of the join, so that the classical coloring is the partition-matroid instance. Conjecture the origin lies in the convex hull of some matroid basis whenever it lies in the convex hull of each color class, provided the matroid refines the coloring. Prove this via matroid exchange arguments that do not depend on the number of colors, unifying the transversal and join viewpoints; the independence complex of a partition matroid is exactly the join of spanning complexes on the color classes.

title: Tropical and order-theoretic analogue of the colorful line theorem
description: Replace real convex combination on the line by tropical (min-plus) convex combination and 'origin straddled by each class' by 'each class attains a tropically small and a tropically large value'. Conjecture an exact analogue of the one-dimensional colorful theorem: a rainbow tropical segment through the tropical zero exists. The core sign-extraction lemma (a class whose hull contains zero contains points on both sides) is an order statement about suprema and infima and should survive to any totally ordered semiring; formalize this over a general ordered structure and instantiate it tropically.
